user_state: Depleted. Running on empty. Guilt about needing to stop. Confusing rest with laziness.

arrival.heading: You have permission to stop.
arrival.subheading: Not eventually. Right now. Before you have earned it. Because rest is not earned.

arrival.heading: Rest is not laziness.
arrival.subheading: It is how the body rebuilds what depletion takes.

arrival.heading: You are running on empty.
arrival.subheading: That is not a character flaw. That is the honest state of a person who has been doing too much.

arrival.heading: Stopping is not giving up.
arrival.subheading: It is what makes continuing possible.

arrival.heading: The guilt about resting is not the truth.
arrival.subheading: It is a story from a culture that confused exhaustion with virtue.

arrival.heading: You don't have to earn this.
arrival.subheading: Rest is not a reward. It is a requirement.

arrival.heading: The body is telling you something.
arrival.subheading: You have been overriding the signal. Today, you can listen.

release.heading: What is the guilt saying?
release.subheading: Write it down exactly. Then we'll look at whether it's true.
release.field_placeholder: What does the part of you that feels guilty about resting say...

release.heading: What are you carrying that is not yours?
release.subheading: Responsibility has a limit. What are you holding beyond yours?
release.field_placeholder: What obligations or worries are you carrying that belong to someone or something else...

release.heading: What have you been doing instead of resting?
release.subheading: Name the substitutes. The scrolling, the overworking, the busy-making.
release.field_placeholder: What have you been doing instead of actually stopping...

release.heading: How long have you been depleted?
release.subheading: Say it honestly. The number is important.
release.field_placeholder: When did you last feel genuinely rested...

release.heading: What would you need to set down to actually rest?
release.field_placeholder: What would you need to let go of to allow yourself to stop...

release.heading: What does the exhaustion feel like?
release.subheading: In the body, not just the mind. Describe it.
release.field_placeholder: Where does the depletion live in your body right now...

release.heading: What are you afraid will happen if you stop?
release.subheading: The list is usually shorter than the fear suggests.
release.field_placeholder: What do you think will fall apart if you rest today...

breath.heading: A breath that asks nothing.
breath.instruction: Breathe in slowly. Breathe out with a quiet sigh. No effort. No goal. Just this breath.

breath.heading: Let the body exhale everything.
breath.instruction: Breathe in gently. On the exhale, let everything drop. Shoulders, jaw, hands. All of it.

breath.heading: The breath of someone who has stopped.
breath.instruction: Slow. Wide. No hurry. Breathe like the day has no demands. Just for this moment.

breath.heading: Rest in the breath.
breath.instruction: Four counts in. Six counts out. Twice. Feel the body getting heavier and quieter.

breath.heading: Soften completely.
breath.instruction: Inhale and let everything rise. Exhale and let everything fall. No holding. Just release.

moment.heading: What does your body need most right now?
What would genuine rest feel like for you today?
What can you put down without it falling apart?
What does stopping look like for you, specifically?
What has been depleting you that you haven't named yet?
What would one fully rested version of you be able to do?
What is the most restoring thing you could do in the next hour?

completion.heading: You stopped.
completion.subheading: That is the practice. Not the plan. The actual stopping.

completion.heading: Rest happened.
completion.subheading: The guilt did not win today. Notice that.

completion.heading: You gave your body what it asked for.
completion.subheading: That is not indulgence. That is care.

completion.heading: The world did not fall apart.
completion.subheading: It rarely does. Rest is usually safer than the fear says.

completion.heading: You listened.
completion.subheading: To the part of you that has been asking to stop. Today, you heard it.

completion.heading: Recovery is happening.
completion.subheading: Slowly. Below the surface. You gave it the conditions it needed.

completion.heading: You chose rest.
completion.subheading: Over guilt. Over productivity. Over what you think you should be doing. That was a real choice.

home_cards.headline: Rest is not earned. It is required.
home_cards.subheadline: You don't have to deserve it first.

home_cards.headline: The guilt is not telling you the truth.
home_cards.subheadline: It is repeating a story you were taught. That story is not yours.

home_cards.headline: Depleted is not a moral failure.
home_cards.subheadline: It is what happens when you give more than you restore.

home_cards.headline: Stopping is what makes continuing possible.
home_cards.subheadline: That is not weakness. That is how the system works.

home_cards.headline: Your body has been asking.
home_cards.subheadline: You have been overriding it. Today, you don't have to.

home_cards.headline: Rest is productive.
home_cards.subheadline: The research is clear. The culture is wrong.

home_cards.headline: You are allowed to stop before you collapse.
home_cards.subheadline: Prevention does not require a crisis.

home_cards.headline: Exhaustion confused with virtue is still exhaustion.
home_cards.subheadline: Calling it dedication doesn't make it sustainable.

home_cards.headline: What you are calling laziness is recovery.
home_cards.subheadline: Those are not the same thing.

home_cards.headline: You cannot pour from an empty vessel.
home_cards.subheadline: You have heard this. Now believe it.

home_cards.headline: The body rebuilds during rest.
home_cards.subheadline: Not during work. During rest. Let it do its job.

home_cards.headline: Slow down before the slowdown is chosen for you.
home_cards.subheadline: Illness, burnout, and collapse are also forms of stopping.

home_cards.headline: You are not behind.
home_cards.subheadline: You are depleted. That is a different problem with a different solution.

home_cards.headline: Permission granted.
home_cards.subheadline: To stop. To rest. To do less than you think you should. Today.

actions.content: Lie down for twenty minutes. No phone. No sleep required. Just horizontal.
actions.why: The horizontal position alone activates the parasympathetic nervous system.

actions.content: Remove one obligation from today's list that is not actually necessary.
actions.why: Depletion is often sustained by doing more than the situation requires.

actions.content: Eat something slowly. Sit down. No screens. Taste it.
actions.why: Eating while distracted or rushing is a signal of ongoing depletion. Slow eating signals safety.

actions.content: Tell one person that you are tired and need support today.
actions.why: Naming depletion to another person begins the social permission to actually rest.

actions.content: Sleep earlier tonight by 30 minutes. Make that plan now.
actions.why: Deciding in advance removes the nightly negotiation with yourself.

actions.content: Take a slow walk. No headphones. No podcast. Just walk.
actions.why: Movement without stimulation allows the mind to genuinely rest while the body moves.

actions.content: Take a bath or shower without rushing. Let the water be the only thing.
actions.why: Water and warmth are among the most effective physical reset mechanisms available.

actions.content: Cancel something optional today. Give yourself the time back.
actions.why: Rest requires cleared time. Clearing time requires the permission to cancel.

actions.content: Sit outside for ten minutes. Do nothing productive.
actions.why: Nature without task reduces cortisol measurably within ten minutes.

actions.content: Read something for pleasure. Not information. Not productivity. Pleasure.
actions.why: The exhausted mind often forgets that enjoyment is a form of recovery.

actions.content: Say no to a request that you want to say no to.
actions.why: Overextension is a primary driver of depletion. Saying no restores energy.

actions.content: Sit quietly for five minutes. No stimulus. Just quiet.
actions.why: The chronically depleted nervous system rarely gets silence. This is direct restoration.

actions.content: Delegate one task you have been doing because you don't trust others to do it.
actions.why: Control and depletion are often the same problem.

actions.content: Let dishes, laundry, or a minor task wait until tomorrow. Consciously.
actions.why: Choosing to let something go is different from neglect. It is an act of self-care.

actions.content: Nap if you can. Even 20 minutes changes neurological recovery.
actions.why: A 20-minute nap provides cognitive restoration similar to a full night's additional sleep.

actions.content: Turn off the news and social media for the rest of the day.
actions.why: Chronic information consumption is a hidden source of depletion.

actions.content: Write down everything you are trying to hold in your head. Then close the list.
actions.why: Mental load is exhausting. Externalizing it creates genuine cognitive rest.

actions.content: Do one thing that is entirely for your own enjoyment today. One thing.
actions.why: Depletion deepens when pleasure is always deferred. This is a restoration mechanism.

actions.content: Ask someone else to handle something you usually handle alone.
actions.why: Independence and depletion are often the same choice.

actions.content: Give yourself an hour with no agenda. Not even rest as a goal. Just free.
actions.why: Scheduled rest with goals is not full rest. True free time is its own category.

actions.content: Eat a meal that requires minimal effort. Give yourself that today.
actions.why: Food labor depletes energy. Reducing it is not laziness. It is efficiency.

actions.content: Lower the lights. Soften the environment. Let the body know the pace is changing.
actions.why: Environmental cues signal the nervous system. Soft light says slow down.

actions.content: Ask yourself: 'What is the minimum I can do today and still be okay?' Do that.
actions.why: Minimum viable output is not failure. It is sustainable operation.

actions.content: Watch something light and easy. Without guilt.
actions.why: Entertainment is a legitimate form of rest. The guilt costs more energy than the show.

actions.content: Write a list of what you have done this week. Not what remains. What is done.
actions.why: The exhausted mind focuses on what's incomplete. Evidence of completion restores proportion.

actions.content: Spend twenty minutes in conversation with someone who restores you.
actions.why: The right social contact is restorative, not depleting. Choose accordingly.

actions.content: Wear comfortable clothing today. Make that a real priority.
actions.why: Physical comfort is a signal to the nervous system that the threat level is low.

actions.content: Say 'I need to rest today' out loud. To yourself, or to someone.
actions.why: Naming a need is the first step toward meeting it.

actions.content: Close your eyes for five minutes. Wherever you are. Just close them.
actions.why: Removing visual stimulus alone reduces cognitive load measurably.

actions.content: Write down what rest has given you in the past. What became possible after stopping.
actions.why: Evidence of rest's value is the most useful argument against the guilt.

What did your body need most today that you gave it or didn't?
What guilt came up about resting today? Where does that guilt come from?
